_comment: R7.2. Villagers standing in the square, placed by scripts/world/village_npcs.gd the same way opening.json places the opening's cast: data describes, code places. `config_key` names a block in data/config/art.json (a tint on Grandpa's or the trainer's rig, never KayKit's Ranger — see art.json's own comment on those keys). `greeting` names a conversation id in data/dialogue/village.json; the prompt label is always "Greet <name>", built by the placer rather than stored here, so it can never accidentally contain "talk" or "choose" — tests/smoke_opening.gd finds Grandpa and the starters by exactly those substrings.
_comment_greeting_when: OF30. `greeting` is what a villager says by default and never stops being that. `greeting_when` is an OPTIONAL, ORDERED list of branches checked ahead of it, each `{ if_flag | unless_flag, conversation }` against autoload/progression_state.gd -- first match wins, no match falls through to `greeting`. Deliberately additive: a villager who gains a role gains a list entry, and nobody's greeting is ever replaced (D39's dual-role rule -- SC12 adds Tam's battle offer as a THIRD entry here, and OF31 gives Mira and Oskar their own lists, without touching this one). Either key may hold a single flag id or an array of them, all of which must hold. No `and`/`or`/`not` beyond that, and no nesting: this is a lookup table, not a quest engine (spec sec19 bans one, and progression_state.gd's own header says so twice).
_comment_sc12_sc13: SC12/SC13. Mira, Oskar and Tam are the Meadows' three Band-1 trainers (spec sec3, D39's dual-role rule made real): once each one's vendor/gift branch has actually been spent, greeting them again offers a CHALLENGE conversation instead -- and keeps offering it, every greeting, for as long as their defeat flag (`defeated_mira`/`defeated_oskar`/`defeated_tam`, encounter_director.gd's SB9 write) is unset. The challenge's last line carries `battle:<trainer_id>` (sequence_director.gd), the same fight `data/config/trainers.json`'s matching `placed_by: "village_npcs"` entry runs. Once beaten, a `_beaten` conversation takes over as their permanent steady state and is inserted ABOVE their old standing vendor branch -- Mira's and Oskar's `_beaten` lines carry the exact same `shop:`/`shop:creatures:` effect their old standing branch always did, so the store/swap stays reachable forever even though the old branch entry below it is now unreachable in practice (kept verbatim rather than deleted, per D39: a vendor branch is never rewritten, only superseded). Tam has no such branch to carry -- his gifts are one-time and both already spent by the time he is challengeable -- so his `_beaten` line is flavour only.
_comment_positions: World metres, on the village square flat (data/config/terrain_playground.json's `flats`, centre [10,-10], radius 18). Chosen and checked against the real runtime structure colliders and the square's four dirt paths (data/config/terrain_playground.json's `paths.routes`, all of which start at [10,-10]) with a headless probe — every position clears every building footprint and every path's 3m width + 1.5m shoulder by several metres, and all three sit far short of Grandpa's house/door/outside markers (~-16,-15 to -9.7,-15), well clear of the smoke test's walked lanes there. `facing_deg` points each villager at the well so the square reads as people gathered around it; `npc_body.gd` turns them to face the player on approach regardless. AMENDED BY OF31: Mira no longer stands in the square at all -- the merchant has a shop, so she is inside cottage_a behind her counter (see her own `_why`). The probe's clearances above still describe the other four.

villagers.name: Mira

greeting_when._why: SG46, spec §9's 'villagers acknowledge the victory'. FIRST in the list on purpose and safely: `legendary_freed` is the last flag the chapter sets, everything below it has already been spent by then, and this branch's own conversation carries the same `shop:goods:mira` effect her beaten and standing branches carry so nothing that was reachable before the Warden becomes unreachable after him (D39's rule -- a vendor branch is never lost, only ever carried forward). Additive as always: the standing greeting is untouched. Paired with `mira_shop_open` so a player who never opened the stall still gets that one-time introduction (and its starting float) rather than losing it to this branch.

OF31/D39. The shop opening: she explains the front room, hands over the starting float on the same line that says so, and ends by opening the store. Sets `mira_shop_open`, so this entry stops matching after the first visit.
SC12/SC13. Her Band-1 challenge -- the introduction (spec sec3). Offered every greeting once the shop has opened, for as long as she is unbeaten. Ends on `battle:trainer_mira`.

SC13/D39. Her permanent steady state once beaten -- carries the SAME `shop:goods:mira` effect the standing branch below always has, so the store stays reachable forever. Ahead of that branch in the list for exactly that reason.

OF31/D39. The ORIGINAL standing vendor branch, left exactly as OF31 wrote it (D39: a vendor branch is never rewritten). Superseded in practice by the two entries above it once she becomes challengeable -- while unbeaten the challenge branch matches first, and once beaten `village_mira_beaten` above already carries this branch's own shop: effect -- but the entry itself is kept rather than deleted.

villagers._why: OF31 moved her indoors: she is the merchant and the owner asked for a store in a villager's house, so she stands behind her own counter inside cottage_a (village.json places it at [18,-2] yawed -135; this is the cottage's local [0,-1.4], a stride behind the counter, facing the open doorway). Was [12,-3] in the square.

villagers.name: Oskar

greeting_when._why: SG46, spec §9's 'villagers acknowledge the victory'. FIRST in the list on purpose and safely: `legendary_freed` is the last flag the chapter sets, everything below it has already been spent by then, and this branch's own conversation carries the same `shop:creatures:oskar` effect his beaten and standing branches carry so nothing that was reachable before the Warden becomes unreachable after him (D39's rule -- a vendor branch is never lost, only ever carried forward). Additive as always: the standing greeting is untouched. Paired with `oskar_trade_open` for the same reason Mira's is paired with hers: a one-time introduction must not be swallowed by the ending.
OF31/D39. The swap explained once: his creatures for yours, no coins, and never your last one. Sets `oskar_trade_open`.

SC12/SC13/SC14. His Band-1 challenge -- the gate (spec sec3): a sturdier team than Mira's, and the fight the South Bridge Key is won from. Offered every greeting once the swap is open, for as long as he is unbeaten. Ends on `battle:trainer_oskar`.

SC13/D39. His permanent steady state once beaten -- precedes, and carries the same `shop:creatures:oskar` effect, the standing swap branch below has always had, so the pen stays reachable forever. Ahead of that branch in the list for exactly that reason -- 'the swap branch still fires' because this entry now fires it.

OF31/D39. The ORIGINAL standing swap branch, left exactly as OF31 wrote it (D39: a vendor branch is never rewritten). Superseded in practice by the two entries above it once he becomes challengeable, the same shape as Mira's own standing branch.

villagers._why: east side, near the two cottages (EV6: the small-barn-and-coop pair became cottage_a and cottage_b). Stays outdoors: his pens are 'behind the cottage' in dialogue and the swap screen is the pen -- OF31 built one interior, not three.

villagers.name: Tam

greeting_when._why: OF30. The blacksmith handover: axe, pickaxe, knife (see village.json's `_comment_of30_knife` for why three, not the owner's two) and the torch line. The conversation sets `tam_tools_given` on the same line as the gifts, so this entry stops matching the moment it has happened -- once, ever, per save.
OF30. The follow-up: he writes down the basic-orb recipe, which sets the flag data/recipes/recipes.json gates `orb_basic` behind.

SG46, spec §9. Placed AFTER his two one-time gift branches rather than first: both of Tam's gifts are one-shot and a player who reached the stronghold without collecting them must still be able to, which a first-position branch would block forever. Flavour only, like his `_beaten` lines -- he has no vendor effect to carry.

SC12/SC13. His Band-1 challenge -- the switching lesson (spec sec3): two creatures of different types. Offered every greeting once BOTH of his one-time gifts are spent, for as long as he is unbeaten. Ends on `battle:trainer_tam`.

SC13. His permanent steady state once beaten. Flavour only, unlike Mira's and Oskar's -- he has no standing vendor branch to carry forward; both his gifts are one-time and already spent by the time he is even challengeable.

villagers._why: south of the well, by the yard fence toward Grandpa's

villagers.name: Quarry Foreman
villagers._why: west of the workshop (EV6; was the big barn), clear of every structure and villager by 8m+ -- NP3, spec sec35. No built quarry to stand him at yet (SD16), so the square is where he waits.

greeting_when._why: OW9 (owner: "Someone else will need to tell you to get wood and build a base camp. They should probably give you a hammer and recipe."). Second use of OF30's one-time-gift route (D43): `give:hammer:1` and `flag:camp_hammer_given` on the same line in data/dialogue/village.json. The Foreman rather than a fourth villager -- CLAUDE.md's 'no new NPCs if an existing one fits', and he already stands in the square with nothing to hand over (his only other branch is `legendary_freed`, flavour-only). Gated `if_flag: recipe_orb_basic` -- Tam's OWN second flag, not one of the Foreman's -- because the owner named the two speakers IN ORDER, gather then build, and the square is free-roam: a player can walk to the Foreman before Tam. Waiting on Tam's flag is what makes the order real regardless of which villager is greeted first, the same way SC12's challenge branches wait on `tam_tools_given`+`recipe_orb_basic` rather than trusting the player's path. AHEAD of `legendary_freed` below for the reason Tam's own gift branches are ahead of his: a player who reaches the stronghold without having collected the hammer must still be able to (D43/Tam's `_why` makes the same argument).

SG46. The foreman's ground is the one D45 says stays baked and partly unhealed, so he is the character who says so out loud -- the honest remainder spoken by the person standing on it. His first `greeting_when` list; the standing greeting is untouched and is still the fallback.

villagers.name: Sela
villagers._name_was: "Rescued Ranger" until SE27, which gave the placeholder a rescue to be rescued FROM and therefore a name to be greeted by. Same entry, same rig, same position -- only the label and the two additions below changed, so the prompt reads "Greet Sela" rather than "Greet Rescued Ranger", which was always a description rather than a name.

place_when._why: SE27/SG46, spec §14. She is Team Tether's prisoner at the relay station until the player frees her (data/config/relay_site.json places that body), and only then does she come to the village. Before SE27 she stood here from the first frame of a new save, which meant a rescued NPC existed before there was a rescue. village_npcs.gd re-reads this gate whenever the flag store changes, so she walks into an already-built square rather than waiting for a reload.

greeting_when._why: SE27/D39. Her post-rescue lines, ADDED above the standing greeting rather than replacing it -- `village_rescued_ranger` stays exactly as NP3 wrote it and is still the fallback, which is what a capture tool or a bare test scene with no flag store will get. In an actual game this branch always matches, because `place_when` above means she is not standing here at all unless the same flag is set.

villagers._why: between the well and cottage_a (EV6; was the small barn), clear of every structure and villager by 5m+ -- NP3, spec sec35.

villagers.name: Kell
villagers._comment: R8.6 / SG46's 'at least one outward spoke gains new dialogue'. She stands at the STORM ROAD's end -- the spoke SG44 reconnects -- and only after `legendary_freed`. Placed from this file rather than from severed_spokes.gd deliberately: that script carries a hard rule that a spoke never explains itself with UI text, and it still does not. Nothing is added to the road, the blocker or the sign; a PERSON walked out to look at a horizon that changed, and she is met the way every other person in the chapter is met. The road past her is exactly as impassable while she talks as it was in hour one, which tests/smoke_boss.gd re-proves after the flag.
villagers._comment_position: At the storm road's own end (terrain_playground.json's spokes.routes[1] finishes at [185.5,49.7]), a couple of metres off the roadbed so she is beside the way rather than standing in it -- the same rule stronghold.json's trainer offsets follow.
villagers._comment_facing: Down the road's own outward bearing: she is looking at the thing she is talking about.

place_when._why: SE27's mechanism, reused exactly: she does not exist in the world before the machinery fails. village_npcs.gd re-reads this whenever the flag store's revision moves, so she is standing there on the walk home rather than after a reload.

villagers._comment_config_key: CLAUDE.md/§21: no new human generation and no new model. `villager_keeper` is the NP4 villager_male base already standing in the square (Oskar's), reused as-is -- she is a villager who walked twenty minutes out of town to look at a horizon, not a new archetype. art.json's own note records that this base has no separable hair mesh, so there is no per-material differentiator to give her; CLAUDE.md's stated fallback for exactly that case is that identical NPCs beat an ugly whole-body hue shift.

villagers.name: Bram

greeting_when._why: R7.9/D39, same shape as OF31's Mira: the inn's own shop opening, told once, ending by opening the store. Sets `bram_shop_open`, so this entry stops matching after the first visit.
R7.9/D39. The standing vendor branch, same pattern as `village_mira_shop`.

villagers._why: R7.9, owner-requested: an inn where the villagers can stay, with an innkeeper who trades. `villager_keeper` is a THIRD use of the same rig already standing twice in this file (Oskar, Kell) -- CLAUDE.md/§21's reuse rule and this file's own Kell comment call that the accepted call rather than a new archetype. Position is `inn_interior.gd::bar_position()` (the gap behind the counter, local [0,0,-4.39]) carried through the inn's own placement in data/config/village.json (`at: [-1.5,-9.0]`, `yaw_deg: 90.0`) by the same rotation formula this file's own Mira position was derived from and verified against (world_x = building_x + local_x*cos(yaw) + local_z*sin(yaw); world_z = building_z - local_x*sin(yaw) + local_z*cos(yaw)) -- not eyeballed. `facing_deg` matches the inn's own `yaw_deg` for the same reason Mira's matches cottage_a's: it points the local +z (front-door) direction the counter faces, exactly as `village_mira`'s entry above already establishes the convention.
villagers._why_vendor: D39's dual-role pattern is a vendor branch AND a later trainer branch; this ships only the vendor half, matching the design ralph/NOTES.md's own R7.9 entry recorded and the same scope call OF31 made for Mira before SC12 later added her challenge. A trainer branch needs a balanced team, a level, a reward and a `trainers.json` entry under `placed_by: "village_npcs"`, which risks the balance assertions `test_trainers_data.gd` runs across the whole roster -- real, separate scope, left open rather than guessed at.

villagers.name: Halda
villagers._comment: TOURNAMENT-1. The tournament marshal -- the person who signs the player into the bracket and opens each of the three fought rounds. A villager entry on the `villager_ranger` rig with her own hair colour, not a new humanoid: CLAUDE.md and spec sec21 both say a new person is a per-material variant on a rig that is already installed, and a marshal is exactly that case. She is a NON-COMPETITOR by design -- Mira, Tam and Oskar are all in the draw, so the person running it cannot be one of them.

hair._comment: Iron grey, distinct from farmer (#5c3a22), smith (#8a8578), ranger (#7a3c22) and Bryn (#c9a86a) so the sixth body on this rig does not read as one of the others wandered north out of the square.

villagers._why_here: The tournament ground: the open north field behind the square, inside the same 14m vegetation clearing at [13, 9] that Bryn's practice arena already uses, 5.0m from the bracket board at [20, 15] and 10.8m from Bryn himself -- more than the two challenge prompts' radii added together, so she never contests his. Facing 215 degrees turns her back toward the square, so she is looking at whoever walks up from the well.

greeting_when._why: FIRST in the list: once the tournament is won, every branch below it is spent and this is her permanent steady state. It is also the line the owner directive asks for -- the one that says a Meadowhart can be ridden and what the saddle costs. The pattern itself is granted by the final round's own `reward.flags`, not by this conversation, so a champion who never walks back here still has it.

Round 3. Ends on `battle:tournament_final_oskar`, and stays offered for as long as the final is unwon -- which is what makes a loss retryable: nothing is consumed by losing, so the player heals their team and greets her again.
Round 2. Ends on `battle:tournament_semi_tam`.
Round 1. Ends on `battle:tournament_quarter_mira`.

Sign-up. The two entry-condition flags are written by scripts/world/tournament.gd from the thresholds in data/config/tournament.json -- they are the ONLY thing this list asks about, so the rule lives in data and this file never carries a second copy of the numbers. The conversation's last line sets `tournament_entered`.
You have the bodies, they are not ready. Told as a reason rather than as a locked door -- she names what to go and do, which is the whole difference between an entry condition and a wall.

The first thing she ever says to a player who has one creature: three, and they have to be a team. LAST of the conditional branches so every later stage of the ladder wins over it, and above the plain `greeting` so a fresh save meets the tournament as a goal rather than as banter.

_comment_tournament_1: TOURNAMENT-1. Halda, the tournament marshal, is the seventh entry and the first villager whose whole `greeting_when` list is a progression LADDER rather than a vendor/gift pair. That is deliberately the existing mechanism and not a new one: the tournament has seven states and each of them is one flag, so the ordered-branch reader `village_npcs.greeting_for()` already written for Mira answers all seven without a line of new code. Order matters and is checked by tests/test_tournament.gd -- champion first, then the rounds newest-first, then sign-up, then the two not-ready explanations.
